 Advertisement 'Just our legally mandated test:' FEMA conducting nationwide Emergency Alert System test Tuesday
 Advertisement Updated: 4:36 AM EST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Amy Lu Washington Correspondent Dominique Johnson Senior Producer 'Just our legally mandated test:' FEMA conducting nationwide Emergency Alert System test Tuesday
 Updated: 4:36 AM EST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Amy Lu Washington Correspondent Dominique Johnson Senior Producer The government is conducting a test of the nationwide Emergency Alert System (EAS) at approximately 2:20 p.m. Eastern time on Tuesday. 
 If you are watching TV or listening to the radio, programming will be interrupted, and you will hear a test message. No action is required, and normal programming will resume once the test is complete. 
 Advertisement The EAS is a national public warning system designed to quickly reach Americans in case of a major emergency. The government is required by law to conduct these tests once every three years to identify any issues. 
 Despite online rumors, the test has been scheduled for months. FEMA acknowledged those rumors in a post on X Monday, saying in part, "No blackouts, no secret emergencies. Just our legally mandated, routine test on TV and radio."
 The test was first announced by the FCC in September. 
 There is no evidence a nationwide blackout is expected Nov. 17. Online claims are unfounded Make WMUR a preferred source on Google Add Preferred Source Share
